primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency prevents lysosomal glycogen degradation, causing glycogen accumulation in heart and skeletal muscle.
vignette: An infant has profound hypotonia, macroglossia, feeding difficulty, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: Muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency causes McArdle disease.
Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes von Gierke disease.
Debranching enzyme deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type III.
Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes hemolytic anemia.
key_expl: Pompe disease is a lysosomal glycogen storage disease caused by acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency.
objective: Recognize the enzyme defect in Pompe disease.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes GAA deficiency with cardiac and skeletal muscle glycogen accumulation.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes acid alpha-glucosidase function in lysosomal glycogen breakdown.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency prevents skeletal muscle glycogenolysis during exercise, causing cramps, exercise intolerance, and myoglobinuria with a second-wind phenomenon.
vignette: A 20-year-old man develops painful muscle cramps and dark urine after intense exercise. Symptoms improve after brief rest and resumption at a slower pace.
distractor_notes: G6Pase deficiency causes von Gierke disease.
Acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency causes Pompe disease.
Branching enzyme deficiency causes Andersen disease.
Aldolase B deficiency causes hereditary fructose intolerance.
key_expl: McArdle disease is caused by PYGM deficiency and inability to mobilize muscle glycogen.
objective: Recognize McArdle disease from exercise-induced symptoms.

sources.title: McArdle disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes PYGM deficiency and exercise intolerance.

sources.title: PYGM gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes muscle glycogen phosphorylase.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency causes sphingomyelin accumulation in macrophages and neurons, leading to hepatosplenomegaly and progressive neurodegeneration.
vignette: An infant has developmental regression, hepatosplenomegaly, and a cherry-red macula.
distractor_notes: Tay-Sachs also has a cherry-red macula but lacks hepatosplenomegaly.
Gaucher disease causes organomegaly and bone disease without this classic infantile cherry-red neurodegenerative pattern.
Fabry disease causes acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, renal and cardiac disease.
Pompe causes hypotonia and cardiomyopathy.
key_expl: Cherry-red macula plus hepatosplenomegaly distinguishes Niemann-Pick A from Tay-Sachs.
objective: Differentiate Niemann-Pick A from Tay-Sachs clinically.

sources.title: Niemann-Pick disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes sphingomyelinase-deficient forms with organomegaly and neurologic decline.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes acid sphingomyelinase function.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes psychosine accumulation, oligodendrocyte injury, demyelination, and globoid macrophages.
vignette: A 6-month-old infant has irritability, developmental regression, hypertonia, and peripheral neuropathy. Brain biopsy shows globoid cells.
distractor_notes: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs.
Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease.
Iduronate sulfatase deficiency causes Hunter syndrome.
key_expl: Krabbe disease results from GALC deficiency and toxic psychosine-mediated demyelination.
objective: Identify the enzyme defect in Krabbe disease.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes GALC deficiency and progressive demyelination.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes sulfatide accumulation in oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, producing central and peripheral demyelination.
vignette: A 3-year-old child has gait regression, hypotonia, peripheral neuropathy, and progressive cognitive decline. Arylsulfatase A activity is low.
distractor_notes: GM2 accumulates in Tay-Sachs.
Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease.
Sphingomyelin accumulates in Niemann-Pick A/B.
Glycogen accumulates in Pompe disease.
key_expl: Arylsulfatase A degrades sulfatides; deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy.
objective: Identify the stored substrate in metachromatic leukodystrophy.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: ATM kinase deficiency impairs response to DNA double-strand breaks, causing cerebellar degeneration, telangiectasias, immunodeficiency, radiosensitivity, and cancer risk.
vignette: A 9-year-old child has progressive ataxia, conjunctival telangiectasias, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, and elevated alpha-fetoprotein.
distractor_notes: Friedreich ataxia causes ataxia and cardiomyopathy but not telangiectasias and classic immunodeficiency.
Nijmegen syndrome causes chromosomal instability but a different phenotype with microcephaly.
Wiskott-Aldrich causes eczema and small-platelet thrombocytopenia.
Rett syndrome affects girls with regression and stereotypic hand movements.
key_expl: Ataxia, telangiectasias, immunodeficiency, and radiosensitivity point to ATM deficiency.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes ATM-related ataxia, telangiectasias, immunodeficiency, and cancer risk.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defects in the Fanconi DNA repair pathway impair repair of interstrand cross-links, causing chromosomal breakage, congenital anomalies, marrow failure, and cancer predisposition.
vignette: A child has short stature, abnormal thumbs, hyperpigmentation, and progressive pancytopenia. Chromosome breakage increases after cross-linking-agent exposure.
lead: Which DNA lesion is poorly repaired?
distractor_notes: UV dimer repair failure characterizes xeroderma pigmentosum.
Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome.
Base excision repair handles uracil and small lesions.
Telomere disorders have a different molecular mechanism.
key_expl: Fanconi pathway proteins coordinate repair of DNA interstrand cross-links.
objective: Identify the DNA repair defect in Fanconi anemia.

sources.title: Fanconi anemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes DNA repair defects, marrow failure, and congenital abnormalities.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: BLM helicase deficiency causes excessive homologous recombination and sister-chromatid exchanges, genomic instability, growth deficiency, photosensitivity, and broad cancer predisposition.
vignette: A child has severe growth deficiency, sun-sensitive facial erythema, recurrent infections, and markedly increased sister-chromatid exchanges.
distractor_notes: Bloom syndrome is not caused by RTK signaling.
Collagen defects cause connective-tissue disorders.
Lysosomal hydrolases cause storage diseases.
Ion-channel defects cause channelopathies.
key_expl: BLM encodes a RecQ family DNA helicase that maintains genomic stability.
objective: Connect Bloom syndrome with DNA helicase deficiency.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of paternally expressed genes in 15q11-q13, commonly from paternal deletion or maternal uniparental disomy, causes neonatal hypotonia followed by hyperphagia, obesity, and hypogonadism.
vignette: A child had severe neonatal hypotonia and feeding difficulty, then developed hyperphagia, obesity, developmental delay, and hypogonadism.
lead: Which genetic mechanism is most likely?
correct: Loss of paternal gene expression at chromosome 15q11-q13
distractors: Expansion of CGG repeats in FMR1
distractor_notes: Maternal UBE3A loss causes Angelman syndrome.
Trisomy 21 causes Down syndrome.
5p deletion causes cri-du-chat syndrome.
FMR1 CGG expansion causes fragile X syndrome.
key_expl: Prader-Willi syndrome results from absent paternal expression in the imprinted 15q11-q13 region.
objective: Differentiate Prader-Willi from Angelman by parent of origin.

sources.title: Prader-Willi syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes absent paternal gene expression at 15q11-q13.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of maternal UBE3A expression in the brain, commonly from maternal deletion or paternal uniparental disomy, causes severe developmental delay, absent speech, ataxia, seizures, and a happy demeanor.
vignette: A 5-year-old child has severe developmental delay, minimal speech, ataxic gait, seizures, and frequent smiling and laughter.
lead: Which molecular defect is most likely?
distractor_notes: Paternal 15q11-q13 loss causes Prader-Willi syndrome.
Dystrophin loss causes Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
HTT expansion causes Huntington disease.
CFTR loss causes cystic fibrosis.
key_expl: Angelman syndrome reflects absent maternal UBE3A expression in the brain.
objective: Recognize Angelman syndrome and its parent-of-origin defect.

sources.title: Angelman syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes maternal UBE3A loss and the characteristic neurologic phenotype.
